claims.claim: gateway21.pelecard.biz and gateway20.pelecard.biz serve the same Pelecard API; the hostname is not an environment switch. gateway21 is the current gateway generation, gateway20 the older one, and gateway20.pelecard.biz/sandbox is a sandbox UI page rather than a separate API host. Both answer PaymentGW/init, PaymentGW/GetTransaction and PaymentGW/ValidateByUniqueKey identically; whether a call is a test or a live charge is decided by the terminal number and credentials sent. Re-probed 2026-10-18 on both hosts with identical responses; a fabricated control path 302s to gateway20 /Errors/Http404 on both.

Only three /PaymentGW paths exist on the Pelecard gateway hosts: PaymentGW/init (create session), PaymentGW/GetTransaction (lookup) and PaymentGW/ValidateByUniqueKey (credential-free validation). Every other /PaymentGW path, including DebitRegular, DebitRegularCancel, Refund, ConfirmDebit, CancelTransaction and GetToken, 302-redirects to an Http404 error page exactly as a deliberately fabricated control path does. There is therefore no refund endpoint under /PaymentGW. Re-probed 2026-10-18: init/GetTransaction/ValidateByUniqueKey answer, PaymentGW/Refund and a fabricated control both 302 to Http404.

ActionType values: J4 = standard sale (default, money moves), J2 = card validation/registration only (no charge), J5 = authorize now / charge later, J5h = enhanced J5. Money fields use minor units (agorot): Total 9900 = NIS 99.00; the dofinity wrapper documents FirstPayment as in agorot/cents. Currency 1 = ILS (dofinity default $Currency = 1).

Callback validation: the dofinity wrapper reads ConfirmationKey from the callback (its README shows $ConfirmationKey = $_GET['ConfirmationKey']) and validates it server-side; no published Pelecard source documents an HMAC or other signature on IPN deliveries, so the skill treats the callback as forgeable and requires matching the stored ConfirmationKey and re-calling PaymentGW/GetTransaction (which Pelecard's own plugin also calls) to read the debited amount from ResultData. Dedupe IPNs on PelecardTransactionId (not ParamX).

Another Israeli PSP's published Bit terms (allpay.co.il, not Pelecard's): payment via Bit cannot exceed 5,000 shekels; all payments per month cannot exceed 20,000 shekels; ILS only; no installments; no saved card (no subscriptions); the charge is made from the card linked to Bit; 10 minutes to pay. Pelecard does not publish its own Bit limits. (In the skill: 5,000 ₪ per payment, 20,000 ₪ a month.)
claims.raw_snippet: Payment via Bit cannot exceed 5,000 shekels.

claims.claim: Israeli Consumer Protection Law (חוק הגנת הצרכן, sections 14C-14E) distance-selling refunds: the consumer may cancel within 14 days, the merchant must refund within 14 days of the cancellation notice, and the cancellation fee is capped at 5% of the order value or NIS 100, whichever is lower. Pelecard handles the money; the tax document (credit note / חשבונית זיכוי) is generated by the invoice provider. In addition, customers who are people with disabilities, aged 65 or over, or new immigrants may cancel within 4 months where a conversation took place during the sale, and certain service categories carry shorter windows, so 14 days is not the complete rule.

claims.claim: Pelecard publishes a live public request builder at gateway21.pelecard.biz/services (ServicesRequestBuilder) listing its server-to-server service operations, including Debit Regular Type (J4), the Authorize (J5) family, the Pending (J9) family, token operations, Delete/Reversal operations, ParamX lookups, Broadcast, 3DS initiation and the error-message lookups.

Pelecard's own public request builder script defines the service URLs for its endpoints, confirming the real paths. Verified paths: /services/DebitRegularType, /services/DebitPaymentsType, /services/DebitCreditType, /services/DebitIsracreditType, /services/AuthorizeCreditCard, /services/AuthorizeCreditType, /services/AuthorizePaymentsType, /services/AuthorizeIsracreditCard, /services/PendingRegularType, /services/PendingCreditType, /services/PendingPaymentsType, /services/PendingIsracreditType, /services/ClearPendingByUserKey, /services/ClearPendingByRecordId, /services/ConvertToToken, /services/RetrieveToken, /services/UpdateToken, /services/CheckCreditCardForToken, /services/DeleteTran, /services/DeleteIshur, /services/EmvReversal, /services/EmvFinishDebit, /services/TrxLookUp, /services/CheckGoodParamX, /services/CheckGoodParamXList, /services/CheckGoodParamXEmv, /services/GetTransData, /services/GetCompleteTransData, /services/GetTransDataBeforeBc, /services/GetTransReportDataBeforeBc, /services/Broadcast, /services/GetBroadcast, /services/GetBroadcastsByDate, /services/GetErrorMessageEn, /services/GetErrorMessageHe, /services/GetTerminalName, /services/ResetUserPassword, /services/CreateInvoice, /services/CreateICountInvoice, /services/CreateEZCountInvoice, /Services/Initiate3DSAuthenticationProcess, /Services/InitiateBankTransfer, /PaymentGW/GetTransaction, /PaymentGW/ValidateByUniqueKey (PaymentGW/init is not in the script; it is verified by live probe, see the hosts claim). The corresponding full URLs on the gateway host (for example https://gateway21.pelecard.biz/services/DebitRegularType and https://gateway21.pelecard.biz/services/GetErrorMessageHe) resolve on both gateway hosts. The builder script itself is served at /Scripts/Services/Sandbox.js. All of these are POST endpoints, i.e. POST /PaymentGW/init, POST /PaymentGW/GetTransaction, POST /PaymentGW/ValidateByUniqueKey, POST /Services/Initiate3DSAuthenticationProcess, POST /services/CheckGoodParamX, POST /services/GetTerminalName and POST /services/TrxLookUp. The script defines 57 distinct service URLs in total: 54 under /services/, plus /PaymentGW/GetTransaction, /PaymentGW/ValidateByUniqueKey and /PaymentEnquiry/CreateLink.

The /services surface uses different parameter casing from /PaymentGW: terminalNumber, user, password, shopNumber, creditCard, creditCardDateMmYy, token, total, currency, cvv2, id, authorizationNumber, paramX, userKey, plus eci/xid/cavv for carrying a 3DS2 result into the debit. /PaymentGW uses terminal, Total, Currency, ParamX, ShopNo and TransactionId.

Money fields are in minor units (agorot). Pelecard's own builder sends the same single shekel as total "100" on /services/DebitRegularType and as TotalX100 "100" on PaymentGW/ValidateByUniqueKey, TotalX100 meaning the amount multiplied by 100. This corroborates the agorot convention independently of the dofinity wrapper.

Pelecard publishes the official bilingual message for every status code through /services/GetErrorMessageEn and /services/GetErrorMessageHe, which take only {"ErrorCode":"NNN"} and require NO credentials. A sweep of codes 000-999 on 2026-08-27 returned 254 assigned codes; the rest return the placeholder UnkownError (English) or שגיאה לא ידועה (Hebrew). Verified examples: 000 operation success / עסקה תקינה., 033 invalid credit card. / כרטיס לא תקין., 036 card is expired. / כרטיס פג תוקף., 308 Duplicated transaction. / עסקה כפולה., 425 Double entry / רשומה כפולה., 501 User name and/or password not correct. Please call support team., 502 User password has expired., 506 Token number abnormal. / מספר טוקן לא תקין., 650 3DS process failed / אימות 3ds נכשל, 302 Debit was successful but merchant is not responding / התשלום בוצע אך אתר העסק לא זמין, 301 Session to Pelecard Timed Out, 303 Merchant is not responding, 011 No Approoval From The Clearing Company For This ISO Currency., 012 This ISO Currency is not Allowed for This Credit Card., 401 Number of payments is greater than the maximum number of payments, 402 Number of payments is smaller than a minimum number of payments, 403 Transaction amount is smaller than the minimum amount, 404 Terminal number does not exist., 503 Locked user., 505 Blocked terminal., 507 User is not authorized in this terminal., 508 Expiration date structure invalid. Use MMYY structure only., 620 This card cannot be used for this transaction., 999 Necessary values are missing to complete installments transaction. Codes 660-680 are ISO 20022 bank-transfer statuses (ACCC, ACSC, ACSP, ACTC, ACWC, RCVD, RJCT, PATC, PENDING, ERROR, CAPTCHA fail, ACFC, CANC, INIT), several of which are successes. Re-swept (English) 2026-10-18: the same 254 codes with identical wording.

Refund endpoint: POST https://gateway21.pelecard.biz/services/ReverseTransaction (path /services/ReverseTransaction). Pelecard's own WooCommerce plugin (v1.5.3.1) refunds through POST services/ReverseTransaction with terminalNumber, user, password, UID (empty), NewAmount (refund in agorot, amount*100), NewParamX (empty), NewPaymentNo (empty) and debitTrxId (the original PelecardTransactionId). It must run on the terminal that owns the original debit, else Pelecard returns 507. The plugin reads StatusCode '000' as success and stores the top-level DebitTrxId as the refund leg id, falling back to PelecardTransactionId. It also uses it to release an uncaptured J5. The endpoint is not in the public builder; live probe 2026-10-18 returned a JSON StatusCode 501 auth error where a fabricated /services path 302s to Http404.

Plugin changelog v1.5.3: refund flow moved from DebitRegularType to ReverseTransaction. v1.5.3.1 fixed refunds on two-terminal setups to use the terminal that performed the original charge, resolving gateway error 507.
claims.raw_snippet: Refactored refund flow from DebitRegularType to ReverseTransaction (no longer requires saved card token)

Consumer Protection Law section 13D(c): a contract in an ongoing transaction ends within three business days of the cancellation notice given under section 14I (six business days if sent by registered mail), unless the consumer named a later date; from then the merchant stops supplying and may not charge for goods or services given after it. (Hebrew: סעיף 13ד(ג), סעיף 13ד, סעיף 14ט.)

claims.claim: Consumer Protection Law section 14I(a) lists the channels through which the merchant must accept a cancellation notice: orally (phone or at the place of business), registered mail, email, fax if the merchant has one, and online for a transaction that can be made online; s.14I(b) requires a site that transacts online to place a dedicated, prominent cancellation link on its home page. (Hebrew: סעיף 14ט, סעיף 14ט(ב).)
